# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches, validated, and only removed from dependency on the old system once financial correctness is confirmed over at least one full billing cycle. The old billing system remains active in read/write dual-run capacity until well after the final user batch is migrated — its retirement is treated as a separate, later project phase, not part of this rollout.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users, ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end reconciliation testing in staging against a synthetic dataset matching production schema, and a rollback procedure has been tested successfully at least once in a non-production environment.

- Select internal accounts and opted-in low-risk external customers (e.g., monthly plans, no active disputes, no complex proration/credits).
- Run both systems in parallel per user; new system generates invoices, old system also generates invoices for shadow comparison but only the designated system's invoice is sent to the customer.
- Manual reconciliation of every invoice line item for this cohort.
- Duration: minimum one full billing cycle before advancing.

## Phase 2: Expansion (25% of users, ~10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completes a full billing cycle with invoice discrepancy rate below the halt threshold (see metrics below), zero critical payment-processing incidents, and support ticket volume for migrated users within 1.5x baseline.

- Broaden to a representative cross-section: multiple plan tiers, currencies, and payment methods (cards, ACH, invoiced/net-terms).
- Exclude highest-value enterprise accounts and any accounts with active billing disputes.
- Automated reconciliation dashboards replace fully manual review, with manual spot-checks on 5% of invoices.
- Duration: minimum one full billing cycle before advancing.

## Phase 3: General Availability (73% remaining users, ~29,200 users, brought to 100%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 sustains discrepancy and incident metrics within threshold for two consecutive billing cycles, finance sign-off obtained, and customer support has been briefed and staffed for expected ticket volume.

- Migrate remaining users in waves (e.g., 4 sub-waves of ~18% each) rather than a single cutover, to preserve the ability to halt mid-phase.
- Include highest-complexity accounts (enterprise, custom contracts, disputed accounts) last, only after standard accounts are fully validated.
- Old billing system remains live in parallel, fully capable of processing invoices, for a minimum stabilization period (e.g., 2 full billing cycles) after the last user batch completes migration. Decommissioning of the old system is explicitly out of scope for this rollout and will be scoped as a separate follow-on project once stabilization is confirmed.

---

## Halt / Rollback Metric

Rollout is automatically paused and escalated for review if, within any phase:

- **Invoice discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5%** of invoices issued by the new system in a rolling 7-day window (comparing new-system invoice totals against shadow/parallel-run totals from the old system), OR
- **Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds 2%** above the pre-migration baseline failure rate for the same cohort, in any rolling 24-hour window.

Either trigger halts further migration into the next wave/phase until root cause is identified and remediated.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-billing of customers during parallel run | Enforce a single source-of-truth flag per account that gates which system's invoice is actually sent, with automated checks blocking dual dispatch | Billing Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Proration and mid-cycle plan-change logic diverges between old and new systems | Run automated shadow reconciliation on every invoice for 2 full cycles before removing a cohort from shadow mode, with finance review of flagged diffs | Finance Systems Analyst
RISK: Payment method tokens fail to migrate correctly, causing failed charges | Pre-validate token migration in a dry run per batch and require a successful test-charge (or token verification) before a user is cut over | Payments Integration Engineer
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during a wave | Stagger wave sizes, pre-brief support with known issues/FAQs, and monitor ticket volume in real time to trigger a pause if it exceeds 1.5x baseline | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Regulatory/tax calculation differences between systems cause compliance exposure | Run tax engine outputs through parallel comparison against old system for all jurisdictions before GA phase, with tax/legal sign-off required to exit Phase 2 | Compliance Lead

PHASES: 3
